# A project can be told not to ask, and new work unmutes it

> A project whose work has ended is noise in a queue whose whole value is that everything in it matters; but a silence you have to remember to lift is the exact forgetting an attention supervisor exists to prevent, so a session that did not exist when you silenced it wakes it on its own.

Applies to `crates/bancada-core/src`, `app/src-tauri/src`.

<!-- archwarden:yours -->

## Context

_Everything between these two markers is yours. archwarden never rewrites it._

<!-- archwarden:end -->

## Considered and rejected

- **A plain `active: bool`** (nothing refuses it) — Silence that only a click can lift. You silence a project the day the work ends and start working there again three weeks later; the queue then says nothing about it, which is the one failure this product cannot have. Forgetting is what it is for.
- **Unregister the project instead** (nothing refuses it) — Loses the path, the workspace, the weight and the machine — everything you configured — to say "not this week". And re-registering is the long form, with a folder picker, for something that should be one click.
- **Wake on any activity, using the log's modification time** (nothing refuses it) — Available for free on both screens, and wrong: a conversation you already dismissed continuing is a write, so every silenced project would come back within minutes. The count of sessions distinguishes new work from work you already declined to look at.
- **Wake on a session whose first event is after the silencing** (nothing refuses it) — The exact rule, and it needs the *content* of every log to find the first event. The work list deliberately reads no content — it costs a process per project per open — so this rule would be computable on one screen and not the other, and two screens deciding "is this asking for me" two ways is how a product disagrees with itself about what needs you.
- **Stop reading a silenced project altogether** (nothing refuses it) — Cheaper, and it makes the waking rule impossible: nothing would notice the new session. It also hides the project from the screen where you would go to bring it back.

## What keeps it

Nothing can. It is a claim about what reaches the queue. A rule can see that `Project::asking` exists, not that every screen counting what needs you goes through it — and the check that matters is that two screens agree, which is a property of two call sites rather than of a shape.
